metadata.title: Open vs Closed AI.
metadata.note: Standalone teaching explainer (~2min). Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'AI, Explained'. ONE insight: open-weight vs closed-weight = how much of the model you can actually access and control — a trade-off between control and convenience, and open-weight ≠ open-source. Hero visual: black box (closed) vs downloadable model (open). Bookends render (composer/verdict/outro); body B01-B04 are house-style 4K PIL cards.

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. You've probably heard people say open-weight AI, and closed AI. But what does that actually mean, and why should you care?

props.command: What's the real difference between open-weight and closed-weight AI models — and which one should I actually use?
output: closed: reach it via an API
open: download and run it yourself

beats.narration_text: Start with closed-weight. The model's trained weights are never released. You reach it only through a company's app or A-P-I, and they control the updates, the infrastructure, and who gets access. Think of it as a black box: your input goes in, an answer comes out, and what's inside stays theirs.

show.event: input → box → output arrows draw (accent on the locked box)

props.caption: weights stay private · access via app or API · e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google

beats.narration_text: Open-weight flips that. The trained weights are released, so anyone can download the model and run it. You can host it yourself, fine-tune it on your own data, and build it into your own systems. But here's a catch worth remembering: open-weight does not automatically mean fully open-source.

props.caption: the weights, downloaded — run it your way

beats.narration_text: So which is better? Neither, really. Open-weight gives you more control: self-hosting, customization, transparency, but you manage the deployment. Closed-weight gives you convenience: it's polished, hosted, and updated for you. It's not open good, closed bad. It's a trade-off between control and convenience.

props.caption: control vs convenience — not good vs bad

beats.narration_text: And here's the distinction people miss. Open-weight is not the same as open-source. A model can hand you its weights while keeping its training code and its training data completely private. You get the finished engine, not the recipe.

show.at: training code and its training data

beats.narration_text: So next time you hear open AI versus closed AI, ask one question: how much of the model can I actually access, and control?

artifactLines: Closed-weight: weights stay private; you reach it via an app or API; the provider controls it.
Open-weight: weights are released; you can self-host, fine-tune, and integrate it yourself.
The trade-off: open = control, closed = convenience — not good vs bad.
Open-weight ≠ open-source: you may get the weights, but not the training code or data.

beats.narration_text: Open versus closed AI. Ask how much of the model you can actually access. Humanitarians AI.
